chunks: As for what al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Ibn Bukayr, from his father, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, he said:

I said to him: I had performed the zuhr prayer on a cloudy day, then it cleared, and it turned out that I had prayed when the day had declined. He said: So he said: Do not repeat it, and do not do it again.

The correct understanding of this report is that he only forbade him from repeating the like of it, because that is the practice of one who does not perform the supererogatory prayers. It is not appropriate to persist in abandoning the supererogatory prayers; rather, that is only allowable in cases of excuses and impediments. And that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ: the zuhr prayer, the obligatory midday salat
key_terms.النَّوَافِلَ: supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory salat
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: valid excuses that justify a departure from the normal practice
key_terms.الْعِلَلِ: impediments or causes that excuse such conduct
key_terms.زَالَ النَّهَارُ: the sun’s decline from zenith, marking the beginning of zuhr time
key_terms.غَيْمٍ: cloud cover causing uncertainty in determining the prayer time
key_terms.لَا تَعُدْ: do not return to doing this again

ai.seo_question: If someone prays zuhr on a cloudy day and later learns the timing more clearly, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of performing zuhr prayer on a cloudy day when the precise time is uncertain, stating that the prayer does not need to be repeated if it was performed at the time of zawal. It also explains that the prohibition concerns making a habit of such conduct, since regularly abandoning the nawafil is not appropriate except in cases of valid excuse.
